name: Pinkish
lede: Pinkish is a deep, dusty [[pink]] drawn from the 2010 xkcd crowd survey, though the plain adjective "pinkish" is far older in English than that survey date.

sections.title: An old adjective, a 2010 swatch
sections.body:
Our library's only dated record for this exact swatch is the 2010 xkcd online color-naming survey, where respondents typed "pinkish" next to this particular cluster of clicks [1]. The word itself is much older: in printed English the adjective peaks in use in the 1930s and rose fastest in the 1870s, long before any survey fixed it to one hex value [2]. Who first used the bare word "pinkish" as a color term is undocumented in the books consulted here [1].

The nearest named colors by measured distance are [[cinnamon-satin]], almost the same shade, and [[blush]], more vivid [3]. [[dusky-pink]] reads duller; [[antique-pink]] redder, and [[red-plum]] and [[dusty-cerise]] both more vivid [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a match for this dusty pink in 9 of them, about 0.04 percent, rarer than 79 percent of the named colors we track, as photographed [4]. A swatch this specific and this far from a pure, bright pink is scarce across the whole archive, so the small count fits that pattern [4]. These are photographs of aged, varnished canvases read as screen colors, not pigment identifications [4].
